title: Efficient bi-allelic tagging in human induced pluripotent stem cells using CRISPR
author: Ren, Takagi, et al.
materials: Here, we used the vectors containing fluorescent proteins as backbone for SIN3A donor vectors cloning. For each DNA oligo, the capital letters indicate the sequences from homology arms, the lowercase letters indicate the sequences from donor vector backbone, and the underlined capital letters indicate the introduced mutations for preventing the cutting of donor vector from CRISPR-Cas9 system. Please check Figures 2A and 2B for the position of each oligo.3.Order DNA oligos for in vitro sgRNA transcription and Gibson assembly as 25 nmol DNA oligos with standard desalting from IDT or other companies. In addition, order Cas9-NLS protein from NEB, Synthego, or other alternative vendor. You can also order Cas9-NLS protein from QB3 MacroLab in University of California, Berkeley.

steps.title: Design sgRNA(s) for target gene
steps.instruction: Identify the genomic coordinate centered on the desired knock‑in site (e.g., 50 bp upstream and downstream of the stop codon for C‑terminal tagging). Use an online tool such as CHOPCHOP or GuideScan to select sgRNA(s) that (i) have the highest specificity with no perfect or 1‑2 mismatch off‑targets and (ii) lie within 50 bp of the knock‑in site (the window can be expanded to 100 bp if needed, but efficiency drops with distance). For SIN3A we selected two sgRNAs flanking the stop codon. Design DNA oligos for in vitro transcription of each sgRNA using the template shown in Figure 1B (forward primer contains T7 promoter, reverse primer contains the partial sgRNA scaffold).

substeps.instruction: Find the genomic region ±50 bp around the intended insertion site.
Enter the region into CHOPCHOP or GuideScan and apply the specificity and proximity criteria.
If no suitable sgRNA is found, extend the search window to ±100 bp.
Record the chosen sgRNA sequences (up to two are optional; one high‑quality sgRNA is sufficient).
Design forward and reverse oligos for T7‑driven in vitro transcription according to the Figure 1B template.

steps.title: Design donor vector homology arms
steps.instruction: Select left and right homology arms of ~500–1,000 bp flanking the knock‑in site. For SIN3A we used a 501 bp left arm (upstream of the stop codon) and a 612 bp right arm (downstream). Design primer pairs for each arm with Primer‑BLAST (or equivalent) and ensure the amplified fragments span the chosen regions. Introduce silent point mutations in the sgRNA spacer or PAM within the homology arms to prevent donor cleavage by Cas9. Design Gibson‑assembly oligos that contain partial donor‑vector sequence fused to the homology‑arm sequence, incorporating the blocking mutations.

substeps.instruction: Use Primer‑BLAST to design primers that amplify 500–1,000 bp regions upstream (left arm) and downstream (right arm) of the stop codon.
For SIN3A, order primers that generate a 501 bp left arm and a 612 bp right arm.
Add silent mutations in the sgRNA spacer or PAM within the arm sequences (see Figures 2C‑E).

Create Gibson‑assembly oligos: each oligo should contain a 5′ segment from the donor backbone (lower‑case) and a 3′ segment from the homology arm (upper‑case), with underlined capitals indicating the introduced mutations.

steps.title: Order oligos and Cas9 protein
steps.instruction: Order all DNA oligos (sgRNA transcription primers, homology‑arm primers, Gibson‑assembly oligos, and Sanger‑sequencing primers) as 25 nmol standard‑desalted synthesis from IDT or a comparable vendor. Also order recombinant Cas9‑NLS protein from NEB, Synthego, or the QB3 MacroLab (UC Berkeley).

substeps.instruction: Place an order for each oligo listed in Table 1 and the Gibson‑assembly set, specifying 25 nmol scale and standard desalting.
Order Cas9‑NLS protein from a preferred supplier.

steps.title: Prepare Matrigel‑coated plates
steps.instruction: Thaw Corning Matrigel hESC‑qualified matrix on ice (>12 h at 4 °C). Swirl to homogenize, aliquot 25 mL of diluted Matrigel into pre‑cooled 50 mL conical tubes, and store aliquots at –80 °C. For each experiment, thaw one aliquot on ice for ≥2 h, dilute with 25 mL cold DMEM/F‑12, and coat culture plates with the volumes shown in Table 2 (e.g., 1 mL Matrigel + 2 mL medium for a 6‑well). Incubate coated plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for ≥30 min before use. Matrigel can be reclaimed and reused if the coating time is <2 h.

substeps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel on ice >12 h at 4 °C.
Swirl vial to ensure homogeneity.
Aliquot 25 mL of diluted Matrigel into pre‑cooled 50 mL conical tubes; store at –80 °C.
When needed, thaw one aliquot on ice ≥2 h, dilute with 25 mL cold DMEM/F‑12.
Add the appropriate volume of diluted Matrigel to each well (see Table 2).
Incubate plates at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for at least 30 min.

steps.title: Thaw and plate iPSCs
steps.instruction: Label a freshly Matrigel‑coated plate with cell line, passage number, date, and initials. Retrieve a frozen iPSC vial from liquid nitrogen, place on dry ice, and add 10 mL DMEM/F‑12 to a 15 mL conical tube. Thaw the vial in a 37 °C water bath until only a small ice pellet remains, then transfer the suspension to the tube and mix 2–3 times. Centrifuge 5 min at 200 × g, 20–25 °C. Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet in the volume of mTeSR1 medium containing ROCK inhibitor (final 10 µM) appropriate for the well size (see Table 2). Remove excess Matrigel from the well, add the cell suspension, and place the plate in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator, gently shaking to distribute cells evenly. Replace media daily with mTeSR1 (no ROCK inhibitor) until cultures reach 80‑90 % confluence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a Matrigel‑coated plate as above and label it.
Remove a frozen iPSC vial from LN₂ and keep on dry ice.
Add 10 mL DMEM/F‑12 to a 15 mL conical tube.
Thaw the vial in a 37 °C water bath until a small ice pellet remains.
Transfer the cell suspension to the tube, mix 2–3 times.
Centrifuge 5 min at 200 × g, 20–25 °C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet in mTeSR1 + 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (volume per well as in Table 2).
Add the suspension to the coated well, incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, shaking gently for even seeding.
Change media daily with mTeSR1 without ROCK inhibitor until 80‑90 % confluence.

steps.title: Passage iPSCs at confluence
steps.instruction: When cultures reach 80‑90 % confluence, prepare a new Matrigel‑coated plate and label it. Aspirate spent media, wash the cells with DPBS (volume equal to the culture medium), and add Accutase (volume per Table 2). Incubate 5 min at 37 °C; if <90 % detachment, extend incubation 1–2 min. Add DMEM/F‑12 (2 × the Accutase volume) to neutralize, gently pipette to create a single‑cell suspension, and collect the suspension in a conical tube, washing the plate once more with DMEM/F‑12 (2 × Accutase volume) into the same tube. Centrifuge 5 min at 200 × g, 20–25 °C, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in mTeSR1 + 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (volume per Table 2). Seed onto the new Matrigel‑coated well at a split ratio of 1:6–1:10. Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, shaking gently for even distribution. Replace media daily with mTeSR1 (no ROCK inhibitor) until cells again reach 80‑90 % confluence.

substeps.instruction: Prepare and label a fresh Matrigel‑coated plate.
Aspirate spent medium from the confluent culture.
Wash cells with DPBS (volume = culture medium volume).
Add Accutase (volume per Table 2) and incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
If detachment <90 %, incubate an additional 1–2 min.
Add DMEM/F‑12 (2 × Accutase volume) and gently pipette to dissociate cells.
Transfer suspension to a conical tube; wash the plate again with DMEM/F‑12 (2 × Accutase volume) and combine.
Centrifuge 5 min at 200 × g, 20–25 °C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in mTeSR1 + 10 µM ROCK inhibitor (volume per Table 2).
Seed onto the new coated well at 1:6–1:10 split ratio.
Incubate at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, shaking gently.
Change media daily with mTeSR1 without ROCK inhibitor.

steps.title: Cryopreserve iPSCs for storage
steps.instruction: Label cryovials with cell line, passage number, cell count per vial, date, and initials. Harvest cells using the same passaging procedure (Accutase, centrifugation). Resuspend the cell pellet in an appropriate volume of freezing medium (e.g., 10 % DMSO in mTeSR1) as per vial capacity. Aliquot the suspension into the pre‑labeled cryovials, place them in a controlled‑rate freezing container, and store at –80 °C for 24 h. Transfer the vials to liquid nitrogen for long‑term storage.

substeps.instruction: Label cryovials with all required information.
Collect cells from a plate using the passaging protocol (Accutase, centrifuge).
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the pellet in freezing medium (e.g., 10 % DMSO in mTeSR1) at the appropriate volume.
Dispense the cell suspension into the labeled cryovials.
Place vials in a freezing container (e.g., Mr. Frosty) and store at –80 °C for 24 h.
After 24 h, move the vials to liquid‑nitrogen storage for long‑term preservation.
